test_title: PYST 20: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 13 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Who has the authority to make laws for multi-state co-operative societies?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The authority to make laws for multi-state co-operative societies is vested in the **Parliament of India**.
 
• Multi-state co-operative societies are governed by the **Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002**, which was enacted by Parliament.
 
• Multi-state co-operative societies operate in more than one state, and hence, come under the purview of the **Union List** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 246 of the Constitution assigns legislative powers over subjects in the Union List exclusively to Parliament.
 
• The Department of Co-operation, under the Ministry of Co-operation, oversees the implementation and regulation of laws concerning multi-state co-operative societies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002:**

 
 
• It regulates the functioning of co-operative societies that operate across multiple states in India.
 
• The Act emphasizes democratic management, accountability, and transparency in co-operative societies.
 
• It provides provisions for registration, management, and dissolution of multi-state co-operative societies.
 
 
 
• **Union List:**
 
 
• The Union List is one of the three lists under the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It contains subjects on which only Parliament has the exclusive power to legislate.
 
• Examples include defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and multi-state co-operative societies.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Co-operation:**
 
 
• Established in July 2021 to promote and strengthen co-operative societies across India.
 
• Its responsibilities include formulating policies and implementing programs related to co-operatives.
 
• The ministry also aims to streamline processes for multi-state co-operative societies.
 
 
 
• **Article 246 of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• Defines the distribution of legislative powers between Parliament and state legislatures.
 
• Subjects listed under the Union List are exclusively under Parliament’s jurisdiction.
 
• Co-operative societies operating across multiple states fall under Parliament's legislative domain due to their inclusion in the Union List.
